newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU agrees comparative advertising law.
newsitem.headline: EU agrees comparative advertising law.

text.p: The European Union has agreed new legislation which will prevent advertisers unfairly comparing the product they are trying to sell with something similiar.

Although, under the rules hammered out by EU governments and the European Parliament late on Wednesday, so called comparative advertising will be allowed, it will only be under tightly defined conditions.

Under the legislation, which EU governments will have 30 months to implement once it is formalised by both sides, comparative advertising is defined as "any advertising which explicitly or implicitly identifies a competitor or services offered by a competitor."

Under the new EU rules this will be allowed as long as the advertisement is not misleading, compares goods or services meeting the same needs or intended for the same purpose and objectively compares one feature, which can include price.

The legislation also lays down that the advertisement should not create confusion in the market place between the advertiser and a competitor or between the advertiser's trade marks, trade names and other distinguising marks.
Nor must it discredit or denigrate the trade marks or take unfair advantage of a competitor's trade mark or designation of origin.
